name: Confluencia
shape: geoBoundaries, the department it is named for

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sémillon, Cabernet Franc and Tempranillo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.top: The topsoil drains fast and warms early in spring. Vines get little water, which keeps crops small and flavors concentrated, but drought bites hard. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
